svg.title: Two-factor authentication with TOTP — SoftTrack web design mockup (#99)
svg.desc: Settings → Security gains two-factor authentication: scan a QR code (or type the key), confirm with a code before it turns on, then save ten single-use recovery codes. Sign-in asks for a code after the password, rate-limited like login. Site admins can clear it for a locked-out user.
svg.text: · scan, confirm with a code, keep the recovery codes
step 2 of 3, confirming before anything is switched on

g.text: Changing your password signs out every other session.
Off. A code from an authenticator app, as well as your password.
Can’t scan it? Type this key:
Enter the 6-digit code your app shows
Nothing changes until this code checks out.
Codes change every 30 seconds. The one just before and just after also work, for clocks
drawn in the browser; the secret
only after a valid code, so a mis-
Each works once, instead of a code. We store them hashed, so this is
the only time you will see them.
Enter the code from your authenticator app
Too many attempts. Try again in 58 seconds.

svg.text: On, turning it off, and a lockout

g.text: Since 27 Sep 2026 · 9 of 10 recovery codes left
Turning it off needs a current code or a recovery code.
Mirrors the admin password reset. Enabling, disabling and clearing
all bump token_version, so other sessions sign in again.

svg.text: pyotp for codes, ±1 time-step of drift, the code step rate-limited through lib_utils/rate_limit.py. Ten recovery codes, stored hashed like invitation tokens. WebAuthn and passkeys,
and enforcing 2FA team-wide, stay out of scope. Security-sensitive: the PR wants careful review, and tests for lockout and drift.
